parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Outline the cognitive explanation of depression (Beck, 1979).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the study by Oruc et al. (1997) about a biological explanation for bipolar disorder.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain two strengths of the study by Oruc et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe characteristics of obsessive-compulsive and related disorders (types, examples/
case studies, measures).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate characteristics of obsessive-compulsive and related disorders (types, examples/
case studies, measures), including a discussion of qualitative and quantitative data. 
Psychology and consumer behaviour

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Outline an associative learning explanation for consumers’ preference for product colour
(Grossman and Wisenblit, 1999).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Outline two methods used to collect data in the study by Porublev et al. (2009) on
gift-wrapping.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Explain one strength and one weakness of the study by Porublev et al.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about environmental influences on consumers
(cognitive maps of retail locations, crowding in retail environments, shopper movement
patterns).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about environmental influences on consumers
(cognitive maps of retail locations, crowding in retail environments, shopper movement
patterns), including a discussion of cultural bias. 
Psychology and health

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Identify two of the measures used in the five-city project on health promotion in communities
(Farquhar et al., 1985).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Describe the study on health promotion in worksites by Fox et al. (1987).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one strength and one weakness of longitudinal research, using the study by Fox
et al. as an example.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about patient and practitioner diagnosis and
style (practitioner style, practitioner diagnosis, disclosure of information).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about patient and practitioner diagnosis
and style (practitioner style, practitioner diagnosis, disclosure of information), including a
discussion of field experiments. 
Psychology and organisations

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Give the equation proposed by Vroom (1964) to calculate motivation.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Outline two non-monetary rewards that are motivators at work.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Explain one strength and one weakness of using non-monetary rewards as motivators at
work.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Describe what psychologists have discovered about group decision-making in organisations
(the decision-making process, groupthink, cognitive limitations and errors).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Evaluate what psychologists have discovered about group decision-making in organisations
(the decision-making process, groupthink, cognitive limitations and errors), including a
discussion of practical applications.
